page: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The processor is equipped with 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.4xlarge demonstrates strong performance in compute and memory-bound operations. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression at 36.52 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.33 GB/sec rank in the top tier, alongside a high Geekbench single-core score of 2383.0 and a top-tier Passmark memory score of 4296.88. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with bzip3 decompression reaching 256.09 GB/sec and Geekbench multi-core scoring 19890.0. For specialized workloads, the server achieves 54.43 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and processes 30.52 tokens/sec for text generation using a medium 7B LLM model.

The server offers high resource density and compute efficiency typical of the ARM64 Graviton family, providing a cost-effective alternative to x86 architectures for compute-heavy workloads. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the absence of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly suitable for compute-intensive tasks such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, database operations, and lightweight LLM inference.
